title: Large language model-based (ChatGPT) versus conventional patient information before planned dental treatment (tooth extraction): effects on anxiety, trust, pain and utilisation of care – a randomised controlled three-arm trial in dental practice
summary:
Many people feel anxious before having a tooth removed. Clear and understandable information beforehand may help to reduce this anxiety and to build trust. This study investigates which form of information works best before a planned tooth extraction.

Adult patients of a dental practice are randomly assigned to one of three groups: group A has a guided question-and-answer session of about ten minutes with the AI language model ChatGPT on a practice tablet. Group B reads an information brochure with the same content for about ten minutes. Group C receives the usual information from the dentist without any additional material. All participants receive the legally required informed-consent discussion with the dentist, and the dental treatment itself is the same in all groups. ChatGPT does not replace the dentist's advice; it serves only as an additional information tool, and no personal data are entered.

The main outcome is anxiety before and directly after the treatment, one day later and three and six months later. Trust in the dentist, certainty about the treatment decision, knowledge, pain, satisfaction and later attendance of check-up appointments are also assessed.
conditions: Dental anxiety (preoperative anxiety) in adults scheduled for tooth extraction

interventions.name: Arm A – LLM-based patient information (ChatGPT): in addition to the routine informed-consent discussion with the dentist, a guided interaction of about ten minutes with ChatGPT (model GPT-5.1, business account, custom GPT with a fixed system prompt) on a practice tablet. Participants type in seven s

Arm B – Standard brochure: in addition to the routine informed-consent discussion, participants read a standardised written information brochure covering the same core content as in arm A for about ten minutes.
Arm C – Control group (usual care): routine, legally required informed-consent discussion with the dentist only, without additional study-specific information.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Tooth extraction under local anaesthesia (without sedation or general anaesthesia) planned in the study practice as part of routine care within the next 14 days
- Sufficient German language skills to understand the patient information and complete the questionnaires
- Capacity to consent
- Written informed consent to study participation and data processing
Exclusion criteria:
- Emergency treatment (e.g. acute pain emergencies)
- Treatment planned under sedation or general anaesthesia
- Severe cognitive impairment or severe untreated psychiatric illness preventing informed consent and/or completion of the questionnaires
- Insufficient German language skills
- Previous participation in this study
